one_line_pitch: A permission-aware hybrid search engine (Elasticsearch BM25 + pgvector) with a grounded, citation-backed RAG layer, where retrieval quality, hallucination rate, and access control are each verified by a runnable evaluation.
problem: Keyword and vector search each miss what the other catches, and picking a blend weight by intuition is guesswork; separately, RAG is trivial to build but hard to trust (hallucination) and hard to make safe (leaking content a user shouldn't see). IndexFlow blends both retrieval strategies with a measured weight, grounds and cites answers with a refusal guardrail, enforces per-document access control on both retrieval legs, and proves each with an eval.
why_it_matters: It demonstrates production-minded AI/search engineering rather than a demo: measured retrieval quality gated in CI, an LLM-as-judge hallucination eval, and permission-aware RAG proven not to leak restricted content. The measurement discipline and the leak test are rarely present in portfolio projects.

architecture.summary: A single Next.js 15 (App Router) application plus a standalone BullMQ worker. Postgres/pgvector is the source of truth, vector store, and ACL store; Elasticsearch owns BM25 keyword search, highlighting, and a denormalized ACL index; MinIO stores original files; Redis backs the ingestion queue; Ollama serves local LLMs. A shared, ACL-aware retriever is used by both search and RAG; identity from Auth.js (Google OAuth) drives an access-control filter on both retrieval legs.
components: LLM layer: Ollama generation + LLM judges (lib/llm.ts, lib/rag.ts)
Next.js UI pages (search, documents+sharing, eval, upload, jobs, signin)
data_flow: Upload: POST /api/documents/upload validates + stores original in MinIO, records owner, creates a QUEUED job, enqueues on Redis/BullMQ, returns 202.

Ingest (worker): download from MinIO -> extract text (.md/.txt/.pdf) -> chunk (~180 words, 30 overlap) -> embed (MiniLM 384-dim) -> dual-write chunks+vectors to Postgres and chunks+acl to Elasticsearch (idempotent re-index).
Search: GET /api/search resolves viewer via auth() -> ES BM25 + acl terms filter and pgvector cosine + SQL visibility predicate -> blendHybrid -> ranked highlighted results.
Answer (RAG): POST /api/answer resolves viewer -> retrieve top-k ACL-filtered chunks -> llama3.2 grounding prompt (cite/refuse) -> stream NDJSON answer + citations.
Sharing: owner-only mutations update Postgres ACL and re-sync the Elasticsearch acl in place so both legs reflect the change immediately.

data_engineer: Built a document ingestion pipeline (PDF/Markdown/text -> chunk -> embed -> dual-store) with idempotent re-indexing and Postgres/Elasticsearch consistency via a shared chunk id.
Wrote idempotent backfill jobs to (re)populate embeddings in pgvector and rebuild the Elasticsearch keyword index (with ACL principals) from Postgres as the source of truth.
ai_engineer: Built a hybrid retriever fusing Elasticsearch BM25 and pgvector via a normalized weighted blend, reaching MRR 0.98 (vs 0.96 semantic / 0.92 keyword) on a labeled 27-query eval with the weight chosen by an offline sweep.
Engineered a grounded RAG layer (local llama3.2) that cites each claim and refuses when context is insufficient, streamed to the UI over NDJSON.
Designed an LLM-as-judge hallucination eval (generator != judges) scoring faithfulness/relevance/citation/refusal; 98% faithfulness / 92% refusal on a 32-question adversarial set.
Made search and RAG permission-aware by enforcing a per-document ACL on both retrieval legs; a leak test proves restricted docs are never retrieved or cited (9/9).
backend_engineer: Built an async ingestion pipeline on a BullMQ/Redis worker with retry + exponential backoff and idempotent dual-store indexing.
Modeled documents, identity, and a group-based ACL in Postgres with Prisma across 7 migrations.
Implemented owner-only sharing that re-syncs the denormalized Elasticsearch ACL in place so changes take effect on both retrieval legs immediately.

interview_notes.short_pitch: A workspace search engine that blends BM25 keyword and pgvector semantic search into a measured hybrid ranking, adds a grounded RAG layer that cites sources and refuses when unsupported, and enforces per-user access control on both retrieval legs — with retrieval quality, hallucination rate, and permission enforcement each proven by a runnable eval. Local models, no API keys.
interview_notes.deep_dive: Next.js app + BullMQ worker over Postgres/pgvector, Elasticsearch, Redis, MinIO, and Ollama. Uploads go to MinIO and a Redis job; the worker extracts, chunks (~180 words/30 overlap), embeds with MiniLM (384-dim), and dual-writes to Postgres and Elasticsearch under a shared chunk id. A single ACL-aware retriever fetches keyword + semantic candidates and blends them (weight 0.4 from a sweep). RAG reuses that retriever, grounds llama3.2, and streams cited answers. Permissions: denormalized ACL + terms filter in ES, SQL predicate in PG, a viewer required at every retriever entry point, proven by a leak test. Everything is measured (retrieval eval in CI, LLM-judge hallucination eval, ACL leak + sharing checks).

verification.repo_scan_notes: Local/portfolio monorepo (~6,900 LOC TS/TSX in apps/web, 15 commits, 7 Prisma migrations). Every claimed feature has working code; correctness verified by four eval/check programs rather than a unit-test framework. No production, users, scale, or cloud deployment. Metrics are from local runs on small labeled fixtures (17 docs retrieval, 32-question RAG) and must be framed as such.
